content: It outlines potential risks, mechanisms of interaction, and recommendations for co-administration. Below is a professional interpretation of the content: 1. Etrasimod and Anastrozole: Co-administration may enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid or consider alternative therapies. The combined immune system effects of etrasimod with antineoplastic, immune-modulating, or non-corticosteroid immunosuppressive therapies have not been studied. Avoid co-administration during and for several weeks after etrasimod use. 2. Etrasimod and Antithymocyte Globulin (Equine and Rabbit): These combinations may increase effects due to aldehyde dehydrogenase inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. The risk of additive immune system effects remains unstudied. Avoid co-administration during and after etrasimod treatment. 3. Etrasimod and Apaziquone: Co-administration may enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing infection risk. Avoid or use alternative drugs. The combined effects on the immune system have not been studied. Avoid co-administration during and after etrasimod use. 4. Etrasimod and Arsenic Trioxide: This combination may prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of cardiac complications. Monitor closely and modify therapy as needed. Etrasimod may transiently decrease heart rate and delay AV conduction upon initiation. Avoid or use alternative drugs due to the risk of additive immunosuppressive effects. 5. Etrasimod and Asiminib: Co-administration may enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing infection risk. Avoid or use alternative drugs. The combined immune system effects have not been studied. Avoid co-administration during and after etrasimod use. 6. Etrasimod and Asenapine: This combination may prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of cardiac complications. Monitor closely and modify therapy as needed. Etrasimod may transiently decrease heart rate and delay AV conduction upon initiation. Avoid or use alternative drugs due to the risk of additive immunosuppressive effects. 7. Etrasimod and Beta-Blockers (e.g., Atenolol, Bisoprolol, Carvedilol): Co-administration may result in pharmacodynamic synergy, potentially leading to additive heart rate reduction. Use caution and monitor closely. While stable beta-blocker therapy with etrasimod did not show additive effects on heart rate reduction, the risk of additive effects when initiating beta-blocker therapy with stable etrasimod treatment is unknown. 8. Etrasimod and Antineoplastic Agents (e.g., Atezolizumab, Axitinib, Azacitidine, Bendamustine): Co-administration may enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing infection risk. Avoid or use alternative drugs. The combined immune system effects have not been studied. Avoid co-administration during and after etrasimod use. 9. Etrasimod and QT-Prolonging Drugs (e.g., Bretylium, Buprenorphine): Co-administration may increase the risk of QT prolongation and Torsades de Pointes. Monitor closely and modify therapy as needed. Etrasimod may transiently decrease heart rate and delay AV conduction upon initiation. 10. Etrasimod and CYP2C9 Poor Metabolizers (e.g., Cannabidiol, Celecoxib): Avoid or use alternative drugs. 11. Etrasimod and Certolizumab Pegol: Co-administration may enhance immunosuppressive effects due to aldehyde dehydrogenase inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. The combined immune system effects have not been studied. Avoid co-administration during and after etrasimod use. 12. Etrasimod and Antineoplastic or Immune-Modulating Agents (e.g., Cabazitaxel, Cabozantinib, Cemiplimab): Co-administration may enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing infection risk. Avoid or use alternative drugs. The combined immune system effects have not been studied. Avoid co-administration during and after etrasimod use. 13. Etrasimod and Other Drugs Affecting the Immune System (e.g., Basiliximab, Belatacept, Belantamab Mafodotin): Co-administration may enhance immunosuppressive effects due to aldehyde dehydrogenase inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. The combined immune system effects have not been studied. Avoid co-administration during and after etrasimod use. 14. Etrasimod and Drugs with Additive Cardiac Effects (e.g., Celiprolol, Carvedilol): Co-administration may result in pharmacodynamic synergy, potentially leading to additive heart rate reduction. Use caution and monitor closely. While stable beta-blocker therapy with etrasimod did not show additive effects on heart rate reduction, the risk of additive effects when initiating beta-blocker therapy with stable etrasimod treatment is unknown. 15. Etrasimod and Drugs with Immunosuppressive Effects (e.g., Capecitabine, Capmatinib, Carfilzomib): Co-administration may enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing infection risk. Avoid or use alternative drugs. The combined immune system effects have not been studied. Avoid co-administration during and after etrasimod use. 16. Etrasimod and Drugs with QT-Prolonging Effects (e.g., Bretylium, Buprenorphine): Co-administration may increase the risk of QT prolongation and Torsades de Pointes. Monitor closely and modify therapy as needed. Etrasimod may transiently decrease heart rate and delay AV conduction upon initiation. This summary highlights the potential risks and recommendations for co-administration of etrasimod with various drugs.
